analysis.evidence: The sons of God are the subject. אֶת־בְּנוֹת הָאָדָם identifies whom they saw, and כִּי טֹבֹת הֵנָּה states what they perceived about them, “that they were beautiful.”
analysis.morphology: Qal wayyiqtol, third-person masculine plural, with prefixed וַ־.
analysis.sense: see or perceive that something is so

analysis.evidence: בְנֵי is the construct form of “sons,” so בְנֵי הָאֱלֹהִים reads “the sons of God,” parallel to בְּנוֹת הָאָדָם, “the daughters of humankind.” The construct relation supplies English “of.” The verb וַיִּרְאוּ agrees with the plural head בְנֵי and does not establish the number of the referent of הָאֱלֹהִים.
analysis.morphology: Definite article הָ־ + masculine plural noun in the absolute state, with no suffix.

analysis.evidence: בְנֵי הָאֱלֹהִים is the subject of וַיִּרְאוּ “saw”. אֶת introduces בְּנוֹת הָאָדָם “the daughters of humankind” as the direct object. The article on הָאָדָם makes the construct phrase definite.
analysis.morphology: Direct-object particle, without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: In בְּנוֹת הָאָדָם, “the daughters of humankind,” הָאָדָם identifies the human community to which the daughters belong. The parallel phrase בְנֵי הָאֱלֹהִים, “the sons of God,” supports this collective reading.
analysis.morphology: Definite article הָ־ prefixed to a masculine singular absolute noun used collectively.

analysis.evidence: After וַיִּרְאוּ (“they saw”), כִּי introduces what the sons of God saw about the daughters of humankind. In טֹבֹת הֵנָּה (“they were beautiful”), the feminine plural pronoun הֵנָּה refers back to the daughters.
analysis.morphology: Uninflected subordinating conjunction with no prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: that (what is seen, known or said)

analysis.evidence: In כִּי טֹבֹת הֵנָּה, “that they were beautiful,” טֹבֹת agrees with הֵנָּה, which refers to בְּנוֹת הָאָדָם, “the daughters of humankind.” וַיִּרְאוּ, “they saw,” presents the women’s appearance as what drew the sons of God to choose wives.
analysis.morphology: Feminine plural absolute adjective, used predicatively.

analysis.evidence: בְנֵי הָאֱלֹהִים is the subject. With נָשִׁים as the object and לָהֶם meaning “for themselves,” the clause reads “and they took wives for themselves.”
analysis.morphology: Qal wayyiqtol, third person masculine plural, with prefixed וַ־

analysis.evidence: The sons of God see the daughters of humankind and וַיִּקְחוּ לָהֶם נָשִׁים, “took wives for themselves.” The verb לָקַח with נָשִׁים as its object expresses taking women in marriage.
analysis.morphology: Common noun, feminine plural absolute, with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: In מִכֹּל אֲשֶׁר בָּחָרוּ, מִן marks the group from which they took wives. The relative clause אֲשֶׁר בָּחָרוּ gives their choice as the criterion, so כֹּל has the force of “whomever” in “they took as wives whomever they chose.”
analysis.gloss: from among any whom they chose
analysis.morphology: Prefixed preposition מִן, with its נ assimilated into כ, plus a masculine singular absolute noun.

analysis.evidence: In מִכֹּל אֲשֶׁר בָּחָרוּ, “from among all whom they chose,” אֲשֶׁר introduces a relative clause modifying כֹּל. The women are the understood object of בָּחָרוּ, “they chose.”
analysis.morphology: Indeclinable relative particle with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: In מִכֹּל אֲשֶׁר בָּחָרוּ, “from among whomever they chose,” the sons of God are the subject of בָּחָרוּ. The relative clause identifies the women they selected as wives.
analysis.morphology: Qal perfect, third person common plural
